full_judgment:
26. Now we have to see the law regarding the burden of proof. In a criminal trial, the burden of proving the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt always rests on the prosecution and on its failure it cannot fall back upon the evidence adduced by the accused in support of his defence to rest its case solely thereon. In criminal cases, it is for the prosecution to bring the guilt home to the accused. The fundamental and basic presumption in the administration of criminal law and the justice delivery system is the innocence of the alleged accused and till the charges are proved beyond reasonable doubt on the basis of clear, cogent, credible or unimpeachable evidence. We find support of the above view in the case of SD Soni vs State of Gujarat AIR 1991 SC 917. 

 31. In order to appreciate the evidence, the court is required to bear in mind to set up an environment in which the crime is committed and the level of understanding of the witnesses. The court must guard against the danger of allowing conjecture or suspicion to take the place of legal proof. Bearing in mind these broad principles, the evidence is requited to be appreciated to find out what part of the evidence represents the true and correct state of affairs. It is for the courts to separate the grain from the chaff. 

 32. The criminal jurisprudence no doubt requires a high standard of proof for imposing punishment on an accused, but it is equally important that on hypothetical grounds and surmises prosecution evidence of a sterling character should not be brushed aside and disbelieved to give undue benefit of doubt to the accused. 

 40. In the instant case, the accused appellant raisec a plea of alibi that they were returning from enjoying cinema and on their way back to their house, police arrested them on suspicion. In case of the plea of alibi, the burden lies on him to substantiate that fact at least to the extent of a reasonable probability. Even if the evidence produced is capable of creating a doubt whether the accused were returning home from enjoying cinema; then the accused persons would be entitled to get any benefit. In the case of Amir Hossain vs State 1998 CrLJ 4315 (Gan) it is held that the burden of proving the plea of alibi is on the accused person. But the accused have totally failed to show any evidence. The plea of alibi has got to be proved to the satisfaction of the court. In the instant case, the defence did not take any step to substantiate their alibi. Thus, the defence is not entitled to get any benefit of doubt.
